title: Four equivalent characterisations of a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of four descriptions of an affine formal algebraic space: being Noetherian; being adic* with every closed subscheme Noetherian; being adic* with the stages of one presentation Noetherian; and being weakly adic with the stages of one presentation Noetherian (statement lines 2557-2572). The proof closes the cycle. From the definition one writes the space as the formal spectrum of a Noetherian adic ring, and a closed immersion from a scheme into it is seen to be affine and to be a closed immersion into the spectrum of that ring, hence Noetherian, which gives the second description (proof lines 2574-2582). Two further implications are immediate from the implications between the types of affine formal algebraic spaces (proof lines 2584-2587). The step from the third description back to the definition writes the space as the formal spectrum of an adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition, uses openness of that ideal to find one of the given Noetherian quotients inside it, and concludes that the ring is Noetherian by the corresponding algebra statement on completions (proof lines 2589-2597). The step from the fourth to the third works with a weakly adic ring, uses that its ideal of definition has an open second power closure, finds a given Noetherian quotient inside that closure, deduces that the quotient by the second power is Noetherian and hence that the quotient of the ideal by its second power is a finite module, and concludes that the ideal of definition may be taken finitely generated (proof lines 2599-2609). The claim is H2: four implications are proved and, while two are immediate, each of the other two is a short argument combining a presentation with an algebra statement about completions or about finite generation of ideals.
